title: Recurring Cracking at the Forward Cargo Door Lower Corner — Request for a Permanent Design Solution
abstract: Skyline International Airways asks for a permanent structural answer to cracking that keeps coming back at the bottom corner of the front cargo door on its long-haul MERIDIAN-46 fleet, after four temporary repairs in two years.

sections.request: We keep finding cracks in the same place at the bottom corner of the front cargo door opening. Four of our aircraft have been through it now, two of them twice, and on the last one the crack had run further than our approved repair scheme allows, so the aircraft sat for five days while we waited for an engineering answer. Our line stations now treat this as a known trouble spot and look at it whenever the hold is open, which is not something we can keep doing. We would like a proper design fix rather than another patch. It has to be something we can put on during a normal heavy check, with the hold linings coming out locally rather than the whole compartment being stripped, and it must not add a new inspection that we then have to carry for the rest of the aircraft life.
sections.background: Our maintenance provider first raised this with us in late 2023 after a routine hold inspection. Since then we have done four repairs across three aircraft, all in the same lower corner region on the left-hand side. Our own reliability figures show roughly 3.8 unscheduled events per thousand cycles on this area against a fleet average below one. We already took the corner fitting upgrade that Aeralis recommended when the aircraft were new, and the cracking carried on afterwards, which is why we no longer believe this is a materials question.
sections.expected_outcome: A design change that takes the repeat inspection off this area for good, available for aircraft we already operate, embodiable inside a scheduled heavy check without a dedicated grounding, and with a clear statement of what has to be done to aircraft that already carry a repair in that corner.

type_data.business_justification: Repeat findings on one corner region cost the operator an estimated 41 aircraft-days over two years across a seventeen-aircraft sub-fleet, plus the standing cost of an opportunity inspection at every hold opening.
